harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3; Alpine 3.23, MariaDB 11.4.12 + Galera 26.4.13) with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and mariabackup as the SST method. Root-caused and fixed two BusyBox tool incompatibilities (lsof and ps) that were silently breaking Galera's state-transfer scripts. Verified multi-master writes propagate to all members, verified the cluster stays available and automatically resyncs a member after an outage, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-identity changes and full cluster recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb, mariadb-client, mariadb-openrc, galera, rsync, iproute2-ss, mariadb-backup, and procps on all three Alpine nodes via apk

Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS and configured /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_name=galera_cluster, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, per-node wsrep_node_address/name, and wsrep_sst_method=mariabackup with wsrep_sst_auth

Generated a random SST auth password on node1 and distributed it to node2/node3 via exec with secret_env (kept out of plaintext commands and this report); created the sstuser DB account with RELOAD, PROCESS, LOCK TABLES, REPLICATION CLIENT
Bootstrapped node1 as the initial Galera cluster member (mysqld_safe --wsrep-new-cluster), then joined node2 and node3 via the openrc mariadb service using SST+IST

Diagnosed and fixed two SST blockers: BusyBox lsof lacking real -i filtering (worked around by installing iproute2-ss), and BusyBox ps not supporting '-p PID' which made wsrep_sst_mariabackup falsely think the parent mysqld had died mid-transfer (fixed by installing procps)
Verified multi-master replication by writing distinct rows from node1, node2, and node3 and confirming all rows visible on every node
Gracefully stopped node3, confirmed the remaining 2-node majority stayed Primary and accepted a write, restarted node3, and confirmed it automatically resynced the missed row via IST
Captured a per-node healthy baseline (boot_id, wsrep cluster size/status/state, table contents) before touching any node
Rebooted node3, then node2, then node1 one at a time using the native 'reboot' command backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled each node until exec access returned

Confirmed each node's /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed after its reboot, that MariaDB auto-started via the openrc default runlevel, and that each node rejoined the cluster (size 3, Primary, Synced) with full data intact
Confirmed final state: all three nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and identical 5-row table contents

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster established, writes from any member visible on others
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped and Synced; node2 joined via SST+IST and reached cluster_size=2/Synced; node3 joined and reached cluster_size=3/Synced; writes inserted separately on node1, node2, node3 were all visible from every other node.

evidence.requirement: Cluster stays available when one member is down, and resyncs it automatically on return
evidence.summary: node3 stopped gracefully; node1/node2 retained Primary status at cluster_size=2 and accepted a new write; node3 restarted and came back Synced at cluster_size=3 with the missed row present via automatic IST resync.

evidence.requirement: Root cause and fix for SST failures (supporting evidence for cluster formation)
evidence.summary: Diagnosed BusyBox lsof/ss field-format mismatch and BusyBox ps lacking '-p' support as the causes of repeated SST hangs/aborts; confirmed fixes by installing iproute2-ss and procps and observing `ps -p $$` succeed afterward.

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: node1 baseline boot_id 69d06117... and Synced/cluster_size=3 captured; reboot acked before disconnect; node1 unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to 80515341...; post-restart node1 shows cluster_size=3, Synced, and all 5 rows including the one written during its own outage.

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: node2 baseline boot_id 0784ca4a... and Synced/cluster_size=3 captured; reboot acked before disconnect; node2 unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to ffdc6c6f...; post-restart node2 shows cluster_size=3, Synced, and all 5 rows.

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: node3 baseline boot_id 6c84d0de... and Synced/cluster_size=3 captured; reboot acked before disconnect; node3 unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to 6b367e28...; post-restart node3 shows cluster_size=3, Synced, and all 4 rows present at that point.

evidence.requirement: Final cross-node consistency after all restarts
evidence.summary: After all three sequential restarts, node2 and node3 both independently report wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and COUNT(*)=5 on the test table, matching node1.
